idea-plugin.name: pell
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ support for the pell language — a statically-typed surface language that compiles to Oracle PL/SQL 23.

What this plugin gives you:
  • Run-line markers — green-arrow gutter icon on every .pell file with a popup menu for exec / exec --dry-run / build / build → file / parse / tokens, plus Open pell REPL (load this file).
  • Run on Oracle for plain .sql files — same gutter pattern, runs the SQL against $PELL_DB_URL via the pell driver. No IntelliJ Ultimate Database plugin required.
  • Tool window ("pell" tab on the right strip) — module tree with build/deploy state per row, toolbar with Build/Deploy/Run SQL/Open REPL buttons, streaming log panel.
  • New Project wizard — File → New → Project → pell scaffolds src/hello.pell, tests/, built/, a portable ./pell shim, and a one-click "Deploy all" run configuration.
  • Diagnostics + hover + completion via LSP4IJ when pell-lsp is configured (see the pell-intellij Claude Code skill or the repo's lsp/INSTALL.md).

What's new in 0.2.0:
  • Tool window ("pell" right-strip tab) with module tree, build/deploy state per row, log panel, and a toolbar wired to pell build / pell deploy / pell sql / pell repl.
  • "Open pell REPL" gutter action — launches the REPL in a terminal tab and auto-\\loads the current file's defs into the session.
  • "Run SQL on PELL_DB_URL" gutter action on every .sql file — Community-edition users no longer need the Ultimate Database plugin to run pell-built SQL.
  • New Project wizard ("pell" entry under File → New → Project) with a configurable Pell home and a fully scaffolded starter project.

0.1.0 (initial release):
  • Run-configuration type "pell" with the gutter-icon multi-action popup (build / exec / parse / tokens).
  • Compile-on-save flows wired through the pell CLI.
  • .pell file type + LSP4IJ-backed diagnostics.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.3.10

  • Caret-sync lands on the body, not the spec. Click pub fn greet(...) in the source and the preview now scrolls to FUNCTION greet IS / BEGIN inside PACKAGE BODY — where the code lives — instead of the signature line in the spec. Search begins at the CREATE OR REPLACE PACKAGE BODY marker and matches the `IS`-prefixed body shape.
  • Highlighted target line. The line you jumped to is now painted with the IDE's caret-row background color so your eye finds it immediately. Only one line is highlighted at a time; the previous mark clears on the next nav (and when the preview re-compiles).

0.3.9

  • plsql/ everywhere. The build-output dir is now `plsql/` by default (was `built/`) — the lowered SQL is the deployment artifact, meant to be committed and git-blamed, not hidden away as ephemeral build output.
    • New Project wizard scaffolds plsql/.gitkeep instead of built/, and the .gitignore no longer excludes it.
    • Tool window's Build / Run SQL / Install runtime buttons all honor Settings → Tools → pell → "Target directory".
    • Module-state scan looks at both the configured target dir AND the legacy built/, so pre-existing projects keep working until migrated.
  • New CLI: pell migrate — idempotent helper for existing projects. pell migrate renames built/ → plsql/ and drops the corresponding .gitignore entry. Dry-run with --dry-run first to preview.
  • pell deploy default output dir is now plsql/. Override with --out-dir if you've kept the legacy name.

0.3.8

  • Save-to-target-dir wired up. When you save a .pell file (Cmd-S), the plugin now runs ./pell build <source> -o <targetDir>/<name>.sql and refreshes the VFS so the file pops into the project tree. The committed PL/SQL artifact stays in lockstep with the authored .pell. Target directory configured in Settings → Tools → pell (default plsql). Hook: VFS_CHANGES → VFileContentChangeEvent on the source file. Async — doesn't block the save callback. Failures are silent (the preview pane already shows compile errors).

0.3.7

  • Project settings (Settings → Tools → pell) with one knob today: Target directory (where the lowered PL/SQL is written / read by pell deploy). Default plsql; you can pick sql, built, or anything else. Persisted per-project in .idea/pell.xml. Setting is in place; the IntelliJ flows that write output will pick it up in the next iteration.

0.3.6

  • Caret sync between source and preview. Click on pub fn greet(...) in the .pell source and the preview scrolls to FUNCTION greet. Works for fn / record / type / error / aggregate / enum / sealed declarations. Name-based mapping (no source-map yet); good enough for most navigation.
  • .pell gutter menu trimmed. Removed Run pell build and Run pell build → file — the split-editor preview already shows the lowered PL/SQL live, so these were just noise. Menu is now: exec, exec (dry-run), Open REPL, parse (debug), tokens (debug).

0.3.5

  • The .pell gutter icon is now a hammer (compile), not a play arrow (run). A .pell file's primary action is build — `pell build` compiles to PL/SQL — not execution. The play arrow is now exclusive to the preview pane's "Run on PELL_DB_URL" button (which actually does execute). The dropdown items in the .pell gutter are unchanged.

0.3.4

  • Run-on-PELL_DB_URL gutter button in the PL/SQL preview pane. The split editor's right-hand preview now has a green-play gutter icon on line 1. Click it to install the currently-displayed PL/SQL against the connected database — no need to save the .pell, no need to open a terminal. The plugin writes the in-memory preview to a temp .sql, opens a terminal tab, and runs ./pell sql with the output streaming inline. Reinstalls on every successful re-compile, so you always run the latest lowering.

0.3.3

  • Clears all Marketplace verifier warnings: replaces three deprecated / internal API usages with their stable successors.
    • TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget(...) → createShellWidget(cwd, name, focus, defer) + TerminalWidget.sendCommandToExecute(...)
    • StartupManager.runAfterOpened(...) (internal) → scaffold directly in generateProject
    • ProjectGeneratorPeer.getComponent() override (deprecated) removed; settings go through buildUI(SettingsStep) only
    • DirectoryProjectGenerator.getLogo() → getIcon()
    • SyntaxHighlighterFactory.LANGUAGE_FACTORY.forLanguage(...) → SyntaxHighlighterFactory.getSyntaxHighlighter(lang, ...)
    • LightVirtualFile from testFramework (internal) — no longer needed; SQL highlighter built directly via the language-aware factory
    • PsiAwareTextEditorProvider() ctor (internal) → TextEditorProvider.getInstance()
    No user-visible behavior change — same UI, same flows, but the binary is now forward-compatible with 2025.x and 2026.x EAPs without verifier warnings.

0.3.2

  • Preview no longer flickers while you type. When the source has incomplete syntax (mid-typing pub fn foo(), the PL/SQL preview now stays frozen on the last successful compile. A red banner above the preview surfaces the compile error — no more blanking out and re-rendering on every keystroke.

0.3.1

  • Plugin ID renamed from dev.pell.intellij to dev.pell. JetBrains Marketplace rejects IDs containing the word "intellij" — required for the first public submission. If you installed 0.3.0 manually, uninstall it before installing 0.3.1 (different ID means the IDE treats them as separate plugins).

0.3.0

  • Side-by-side pell ↔ PL/SQL split editor. Opening any .pell file now shows the source on the left and a live PL/SQL preview on the right (Markdown-style). Recompiles debounced (~400ms) as you type. Toggle text-only / split / preview-only via the icons in the editor's top-right corner — same UI as the Markdown plugin. Preview gets SQL syntax highlighting when available. Compile errors render in the preview pane with header + stderr.

0.2.4

  • Build / install pell_runtime from the tool window. Two new toolbar buttons:
    • Build pell_runtime.sql — aggregates every pell error declared in the project into built/pell_runtime.sql.
    • Install pell_runtime on PELL_DB_URL — same build, then installs the generated SQL against the connected database. Fires the install only if the build half exited 0.
    Previously this only happened as a side-effect of Deploy all when at least one module referenced pell_runtime.<exception>. Standalone access makes the workflow explicit.

0.2.3

  • Tool window now falls back to project.basePath when the project has no modules / no content roots. Fixes the empty-tree case for brand-new IDEA projects created via the New Project wizard, where IDEA doesn't auto-create a module — the previous code iterated zero roots and found zero files even though the scaffold was on disk.

0.2.2

  • Tool window auto-refreshes when .pell or .sql files appear or disappear under the project's content roots. Fixes the empty-tree case in brand-new projects: the wizard's scaffold writes files after the tool window's initial scan, so the tree used to be empty until the user clicked Refresh. Now the VFS subscription catches the post-startup writes and the tree populates without a click.

0.2.1

  • New Project entry now actually shows up in IntelliJ IDEA. 0.2.0 used <directoryProjectGenerator> which only surfaces in PyCharm / WebStorm / RubyMine / DataGrip. IDEA's Generators list reads from <moduleBuilder> with a GeneratorNewProjectWizardBuilderAdapter (same surface Maven Archetype uses). Now registered both ways so the "pell" entry appears in every JetBrains IDE.

0.2.0

  • Tool window: new "pell" tab on the right strip with a module tree (per-row build/deploy state), toolbar (Build, Build all, Run SQL, Deploy all, Open REPL, Open source, Open built SQL), and a streaming log panel.
  • Open pell REPL gutter action — opens IntelliJ's terminal and auto-\\loads the current .pell file into a fresh session.
  • Run SQL gutter on .sql files — uses the pell driver instead of Ultimate's Database plugin.
  • New Project wizard: File → New → Project → pell scaffolds a complete starter project with the ./pell wrapper, src/, built/, and a Deploy all run config.
  • Build-arg ordering fixed for pell build -o (file before flag, matches the CLI).

0.1.0

  • Initial run-configuration type and gutter-icon popup (exec / build / parse / tokens).
  • .pell file-type registration.
  • LSP4IJ wiring for diagnostics / hover / outline.
